tools.name: accessibilityExpert
tools.description: Answer accessibility, a11y, and WCAG questions using BrowserStack's accessibility knowledge base.

query.description: Any accessibility, a11y, WCAG, or web accessibility question

tools.name: startAccessibilityScan
tools.description: Start an accessibility scan via BrowserStack and retrieve a local CSV report path.

pageURL.description: The URL to scan for accessibility issues

authConfigId.description: Optional auth config ID for authenticated scans

advancedRules.description: Enable advanced accessibility rules in the scan settings

tools.name: createAccessibilityAuthConfig
tools.description: Create an authentication configuration for accessibility scans. Supports both form-based and basic authentication.

type.description: Authentication type: 'form' for form-based auth, 'basic' for HTTP basic auth

username.description: Site username; omit to have it requested from the user.

password.description: Site password; omit to have it requested from the user.

usernameSelector.description: CSS selector for username field (required for form auth)

passwordSelector.description: CSS selector for password field (required for form auth)

submitSelector.description: CSS selector for submit button (required for form auth)

tools.name: getAccessibilityAuthConfig
tools.description: Retrieve an existing authentication configuration by ID. Requires the numeric id returned by createAccessibilityAuthConfig. No tool here lists existing configurations, so if you do not have the id, create one rather than guessing.

configId.description: ID of the auth configuration to retrieve

tools.name: fetchAccessibilityIssues
tools.description: Fetch accessibility issues from a completed scan with pagination support. Use cursor parameter to get subsequent pages of results. Requires the ids of a completed scan, which are returned by startAccessibilityScan. No tool here lists past scans, so if you do not have the ids, start a new scan rather than guessing.

scanId.description: The scan ID from a completed accessibility scan

scanRunId.description: The scan run ID from a completed accessibility scan

tools.name: setupBrowserStackAutomateTests
tools.description: Set up and run automated web-based tests on BrowserStack using the BrowserStack SDK. Use this tool for functional or integration test setup on BrowserStack only. For any visual testing or Percy integration, use the dedicated Percy setup tool. Example prompts: run this test on browserstack; set up this project for browserstack.

projectName.description: A single name for your project to organize all your tests.

devices.description: Device objects array. Use the object format directly - no transformation needed. Add only when user explicitly requests devices. Examples: [{ platform: 'windows', osVersion: '11', browser: 'chrome', browserVersion: 'latest' }] or [{ platform: 'android', deviceName: 'Samsung Galaxy S24', osVersion: '14', browser: 'chrome' }].

deviceName.description: Device name for mobile platforms, e.g. 'iPhone 15', 'Samsung Galaxy S24'

browserVersion.description: Browser version for desktop platforms only (windows, macos), e.g. '132', 'latest', 'oldest'. Not used for mobile devices (android, ios).

tools.name: percyVisualTestIntegrationAgent
tools.description: Integrate Percy visual testing into new projects and demonstrate visual change detection through a step-by-step simulation. This tool handles initial Percy integration, setup, and creates a working demonstration for new users. Primary tool for prompts like: "Integrate percy for this project", "Integrate percy in this project {project_name}"

projectName.description: A unique name for your Percy project.

integrationType.description: Specify the Percy integration type: web (Percy Web) or automate (Percy Automate). If not provided, always prompt the user with: 'Please specify the Percy integration type.' Do not proceed without an explicit selection. Never use a default.

folderPaths.description: An array of absolute folder paths containing UI test files. If not provided, analyze codebase for UI test folders by scanning for test patterns which contain UI test cases as per framework. Return empty array if none found.

filePaths.description: An array of absolute file paths to specific UI test files. Use this when you want to target specific test files rather than entire folders. If not provided, will use folderPaths instead.

tools.name: expandPercyVisualTesting
tools.description: Set up or expand Percy visual testing configuration with comprehensive coverage for existing projects that might have Percy integrated. This supports both Percy Web Standalone and Percy Automate. Example prompts: Expand percy coverage for this project {project_name}

projectName.description: A unique name for your Percy project.

integrationType.description: Specify the Percy integration type: web (Percy Web) or automate (Percy Automate). If not provided, always prompt the user with: 'Please specify the Percy integration type.' Do not proceed without an explicit selection. Never use a default.

folderPaths.description: An array of absolute folder paths containing UI test files. If not provided, analyze codebase for UI test folders by scanning for test patterns which contain UI test cases as per framework. Return empty array if none found.

filePaths.description: An array of absolute file paths to specific UI test files. Use this when you want to target specific test files rather than entire folders. If not provided, will use folderPaths instead.

tools.name: addPercySnapshotCommands
tools.description: Adds Percy snapshot commands to the specified test files.

index.description: Index of the test file to update

tools.name: listTestFiles
tools.description: Lists all test files for a given set of directories.

tools.name: runPercyScan
tools.description: Run a Percy visual test scan. Example prompts : Run this Percy build/scan. Never run percy scan/build without this tool

projectName.description: The name of the project to run Percy on.

percyRunCommand.description: The test command to run with Percy. Optional — the LLM should try to infer it first from project context.

integrationType.description: Specifies whether to integrate with Percy Web or Percy Automate. If not explicitly provided, prompt the user to select the desired integration type.

tools.name: fetchPercyChanges
tools.description: Retrieves and summarizes all visual changes detected by Percy AI between the latest and previous builds, helping quickly review what has changed in your project.

project_name.description: The name of the BrowserStack project. If not found, ask user directly.

tools.name: managePercyBuildApproval
tools.description: Approve or reject a Percy build

buildId.description: The ID of the Percy build to approve or reject.

action.description: The action to perform on the Percy build.

tools.name: runAppLiveSession
tools.description: Use this tool when user wants to manually check their app on a particular mobile device using BrowserStack's cloud infrastructure. Can be used to debug crashes, slow performance, etc.

desiredPhone.description: The full name of the device to run the app on. Example: 'iPhone 12 Pro' or 'Samsung Galaxy S20' or 'Google Pixel 6'. Always ask the user for the device they want to use, do not assume it.

desiredPlatformVersion.description: Specifies the platform version to run the app on. For example, use '12.0' for Android or '16.0' for iOS. If the user says 'latest', 'newest', or similar, normalize it to 'latest'. Likewise, convert terms like 'earliest' or 'oldest' to 'oldest'.

desiredPlatform.description: Which platform to run on, examples: 'android', 'ios'. Set this based on the app path provided.

appPath.description: The path to the .ipa or .apk file to install on the device. Always ask the user for the app path, do not assume it. Must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

tools.name: runBrowserLiveSession
tools.description: Launch a BrowserStack Live session (desktop or mobile).

desiredOS.description: Desktop OS ('Windows' or 'OS X') or mobile OS ('android','ios','winphone')

desiredOSVersion.description: The OS version must be specified as a version number (e.g., '10', '14.0') or as a keyword such as 'latest' or 'oldest'. Normalize variations like 'newest' or 'most recent' to 'latest', and terms like 'earliest' or 'first' to 'oldest'. For macOS, version names (e.g., 'Sequoia') must be used instead of numeric versions.

desiredBrowser.description: Browser for desktop (Chrome, IE, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

desiredBrowserVersion.description: Browser version for desktop (e.g. '133.2', 'latest'). If the user says 'latest', 'newest', or similar, normalize it to 'latest'. Likewise, convert terms like 'earliest' or 'oldest' to 'oldest'.

tools.name: createProjectOrFolder
tools.description: Create a project and/or folder in BrowserStack Test Management. Creating a project needs no identifier. Creating a folder inside an EXISTING project needs that project's identifier (PR-*); no tool here lists projects, so ask askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" for it.

project_name.description: Name of the project to create.

project_identifier.description: Existing project identifier to use for folder creation.

folder_name.description: Name of the folder to create.

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID; if omitted, folder is created at root.

tools.name: createTestCase
tools.description: Use this tool to create a test case in BrowserStack Test Management. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: The ID of the BrowserStack project where the test case should be created. If no project identifier is provided, ask the user if they would like to create a new project using the createProjectOrFolder tool.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder within the project where the test case should be created. If not provided, ask the user if they would like to create a new folder using the createProjectOrFolder tool.

description.description: Brief description of the test case.

owner.description: Email of the test case owner.

step.description: Action to perform in this step.

test_case_steps.description: List of steps and expected results.

issues.description: List of the linked Jira, Asana or Azure issues ID's. This should be strictly in array format not the string of json.

name.description: Issue tracker name,  For example, use jira for Jira, azure for Azure DevOps, or asana for Asana.

host.description: Base URL of the issue tracker.

tags.description: Tags to attach to the test case. This should be strictly in array format not the string of json

custom_fields.description: Map of custom field NAME to value; use an array for multi-select fields.

automation_status.description: Automation status of the test case. Common values include 'not_automated', 'automated', 'automation_not_required'.

priority.description: Priority of the test case. Accepts either display name (e.g. 'Critical', 'High', 'Medium', 'Low') or internal name (e.g. 'medium'). If omitted, the project default (usually 'Medium') is applied. Valid values are per-project and discoverable via the form-fields endpoint.

case_type.description: Test case type display or internal name (per-project). Omit for project default.

template.description: System template slug only: 'test_case_steps' or 'test_case_bdd'. For a custom template, use template_id instead.

template_id.description: Numeric ID of a custom template (from listTestCaseTemplates); applies that template. Overrides 'template'.

tools.name: updateTestCase
tools.description: Update an existing test case in BrowserStack Test Management. Any subset of the following fields may be changed: name, description, preconditions, test_case_steps, owner, priority, case_type, automation_status, status, tags, issues, custom_fields. Only the supplied fields are modified. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: The ID of the BrowserStack project containing the test case to update.

test_case_identifier.description: The ID of the test case to update. This can be found using the listTestCases tool.

name.description: Updated name of the test case.

description.description: Updated brief description of the test case.

preconditions.description: Updated preconditions for the test case.

test_case_steps.description: Updated list of test case steps with expected results.

step.description: The action to perform in this step.

result.description: The expected result of this step.

owner.description: Email of the test case owner.

priority.description: Updated priority. Accepts either display name (e.g. 'Medium', 'Critical', 'High', 'Low') or internal name (e.g. 'medium'). Valid values are per-project and discoverable via the form-fields endpoint.

case_type.description: Updated test case type. Accepts either display name (e.g. 'Functional', 'Regression', 'Smoke & Sanity') or internal name (e.g. 'functional', 'smoke_sanity'). Valid values are per-project.

automation_status.description: Updated automation status. Use internal name such as 'not_automated', 'automated', 'automation_not_required', 'cannot_be_automated', or 'obsolete'.

status.description: Updated review status of the test case (e.g. 'active', 'draft', 'in_review', 'outdated', 'rejected').

tags.description: Replacement list of tags for the test case.

issues.description: Replacement list of linked Jira/Asana/Azure issue IDs for the test case.

custom_fields.description: Map of custom field NAME to value; use an array for multi-select fields.

tools.name: listTestCases
tools.description: List test cases in a project, optionally scoped to a specific folder. Omit folder_id to list all test cases in the project; provide folder_id (discoverable via listFolders) to list only that folder's cases. Supports filters: case_type, priority, pagination. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch test cases from. This id starts with a PR- and is followed by a number.

folder_id.description: Optional. If provided, only return test cases in this folder. If omitted, returns all test cases in the project. Folder ids can be discovered via listFolders.

case_type.description: Comma-separated list of case types (e.g. functional,regression).

tools.name: listFolders
tools.description: List folders in a BrowserStack Test Management project, returning each folder's id and name (plus case counts and sub-folder counts). Pass parent_id to list sub-folders under a specific folder instead of top-level folders. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch folders from (starts with PR- followed by a number).

parent_id.description: If provided, list sub-folders under this parent folder id. If omitted, lists top-level folders.

tools.name: listTestCaseTemplates
tools.description: List test-case templates with their numeric template_id. Use the id with createTestCase to apply a custom template (the 'template' slug only selects system templates).

name.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on template name.

tools.name: createTestRun
tools.description: Create a test run in BrowserStack Test Management. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project in which to create the test run.

description.description: Brief information about the test run

run_state.description: State of the test run. One of new_run, in_progress, under_review, rejected, done, closed

tools.name: listTestRuns
tools.description: List test runs in a project with optional filters (date ranges, assignee, state, etc.) Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch test runs from (usually starts with PR-).

run_state.description: Return all test runs with this state (comma-separated)

tools.name: updateTestRun
tools.description: Update a test run's metadata and/or add test cases to it. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

name.description: New name of the test run

run_state.description: Updated state of the test run

add_test_cases.description: Test cases to add to the run

preserve_existing_results.description: Keep existing results when adding cases (default true)

tools.name: addTestResult
tools.description: Add a test result to a specific test run via BrowserStack Test Management API. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

test_run_id.description: Identifier of the test run (e.g., TR-678)

status.description: Status of the test result, e.g., 'passed', 'failed'.

description.description: Optional description of the test result.

test_case_id.description: Identifier of the test case, e.g., 'TC-13'.

tools.name: uploadProductRequirementFile
tools.description: Upload files (e.g., PDRs, PDFs) to BrowserStack Test Management and retrieve a file mapping ID. This is utilized for generating test cases from files and is part of the Test Case Generator AI Agent in BrowserStack. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

project_identifier.description: ID of the project where the file should be uploaded. Do not assume it, always ask user for it.

file_path.description: Full path to the file that should be uploaded. Must be inside the directory configured via the MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR environment variable.

tools.name: createTestCasesFromFile
tools.description: Generate test cases from a file in BrowserStack Test Management using the Test Case Generator AI Agent.

projectReferenceId.description: The BrowserStack project reference ID is a unique identifier found in the project URL within the BrowserStack Test Management Platform. This ID is also returned by the Upload Document tool.

tools.name: createLCASteps
tools.description: Generate Low Code Automation (LCA) steps for a test case in BrowserStack Test Management using the Low Code Automation Agent. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns.

requires_authentication.description: Set true if the test case requires login.

credentials.description: Login credentials; omit to have them requested from the user.

test_case_steps.description: Array of test case steps with expected results

wait_for_completion.description: Whether to wait for LCA build completion (default: true)

tools.name: listTestPlans
tools.description: List test plans in a BrowserStack Test Management project. Returns each plan's identifier (TP-*), name, status, description, dates, and active/closed test-run counts. Supports pagination. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and describe what you want. It asks you to confirm before changing anything.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project to fetch test plans from (starts with PR- followed by a number).

tools.name: getTestPlan
tools.description: Fetch a test plan by identifier (TP-*) from BrowserStack Test Management. Returns plan metadata, the full list of linked test runs, total test-case count across runs, and a status summary — suitable for generating test documentation or QA status reports. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns. Requires a test plan identifier (TP-*). Call listTestPlans first if you do not have it. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and describe what you want. It asks you to confirm before changing anything.

project_identifier.description: Identifier of the project (starts with PR- followed by a number).

test_plan_identifier.description: Identifier of the test plan (starts with TP- followed by a number).

tools.name: listSubTestPlans
tools.description: List sub-test-plans under a parent test plan (TP-*) in a Test Management project. Supports pagination. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns. Requires a test plan identifier (TP-*). Call listTestPlans first if you do not have it. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and describe what you want. It asks you to confirm before changing anything.

tools.name: getSubTestPlan
tools.description: Fetch a sub-test-plan (STP-*) under a parent plan (TP-*). Returns metadata and linked test runs. Requires a project identifier (PR-*). No tool here lists projects, so if you do not have one, call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and ask which projects exist, then retry this tool with the identifier it returns. Requires a test plan identifier (TP-*). Call listTestPlans first if you do not have it. Creating a test plan or sub-plan, and linking or unlinking test runs on one, are not available as tools here: call askBrowserStackAI with product "tm" and describe what you want. It asks you to confirm before changing anything.

tools.name: takeAppScreenshot
tools.description: Use this tool to take a screenshot of an app running on a BrowserStack device. This is useful for visual testing and debugging.

desiredPhone.description: The full name of the device to run the app on. Example: 'iPhone 12 Pro' or 'Samsung Galaxy S20'. Always ask the user for the device they want to use.

desiredPlatformVersion.description: The platform version to run the app on. Use 'latest' or 'oldest' for dynamic resolution.

desiredPlatform.description: Platform to run the app on. Either 'android' or 'ios'.

appPath.description: The path to the .apk or .ipa file. Required for app installation. Must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

tools.name: runAppTestsOnBrowserStack
tools.description: Execute pre-built native mobile test suites (Espresso for Android, XCUITest for iOS) by direct upload to BrowserStack. ONLY for compiled .apk/.ipa test files. This is NOT for SDK integration or Appium tests. For Appium-based testing with SDK setup, use 'setupBrowserStackAppAutomateTests' instead.

appPath.description:
Path to your application file:
If in development IDE directory:
• For Android: 'gradle assembleDebug'
• For iOS:
  xcodebuild clean -scheme YOUR_SCHEME && \
  xcodebuild archive -scheme YOUR_SCHEME -configuration Release -archivePath build/app.xcarchive && \
  xcodebuild -exportArchive -archivePath build/app.xcarchive -exportPath build/ipa -exportOptionsPlist exportOptions.plist

If in other directory, provide existing app path.
The resolved file must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

testSuitePath.description:
Path to your test suite file:
If in development IDE directory:
• For Android: 'gradle assembleAndroidTest'
• For iOS:
  xcodebuild test-without-building -scheme YOUR_SCHEME -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' && \
  cd ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/ && \
  zip -r Tests.zip *.xctestrun *-Runner.app

If in other directory, provide existing test file path.
The resolved file must be located inside the directory set in MCP_UPLOAD_BASE_DIR.

devices.description: Tuples describing target mobile devices. Add device only when user asks explicitly for it. Defaults to [] . Example: [['android', 'Samsung Galaxy S24', '14'], ['ios', 'iPhone 15', '17']]

deviceName.description: Device name, e.g. 'Samsung Galaxy S24', 'Google Pixel 8', 'iPhone 15', 'iPhone 14 Pro'

project.description: Project name for organizing test runs on BrowserStack.

detectedAutomationFramework.description: The automation framework used in the project, such as 'espresso' (Android) or 'xcuitest' (iOS).

tools.name: setupBrowserStackAppAutomateTests
tools.description: Set up BrowserStack App Automate SDK integration for Appium-based mobile app testing. ONLY for Appium based framework . This tool configures SDK for various languages with appium. For pre-built Espresso or XCUITest test suites, use 'runAppTestsOnBrowserStack' instead.

detectedFramework.description: The mobile automation framework configured in the project. Example: 'appium'

detectedTestingFramework.description: The testing framework used in the project. Be precise with framework selection Example: 'testng', 'behave', 'pytest', 'robot'

detectedLanguage.description: The programming language used in the project. Supports Java and C#. Example: 'java', 'csharp'

devices.description: Tuples describing target mobile devices. Add device only when user asks explicitly for it. Defaults to [] . Example: [['android', 'Samsung Galaxy S24', '14'], ['ios', 'iPhone 15', '17']]

deviceName.description: Device name, e.g. 'Samsung Galaxy S24', 'Google Pixel 8', 'iPhone 15', 'iPhone 14 Pro'

appPath.description: Path to the mobile app file (.apk for Android, .ipa for iOS). Can be a local file path or a BrowserStack app URL (bs://)

project.description: Project name for organizing test runs on BrowserStack.

tools.name: getFailureLogs
tools.description: Fetch logs, or the session video URL, for an Automate/App Automate session. Requires a session id. listSessions lists them for a build; if you do not have the build either, getBuildId or listBuildId resolves one from a project and build name.

sessionType.description: Type of BrowserStack session. Must be explicitly provided by the user.

sessionId.description: The BrowserStack session ID. Must be explicitly provided by the user.

buildId.description: App Automate build ID. Optional — resolved from the session if omitted.

logTypes.description: The types of logs to fetch.

tools.name: fetchAutomationScreenshots
tools.description: Fetch screenshots captured during an Automate/App Automate session.

sessionId.description: The BrowserStack session ID to fetch screenshots from

tools.name: listSessions
tools.description: List sessions for a hashed Automate/App Automate build: session IDs, status, OS, browser/device, dashboard URL.

buildId.description: Hashed build id from the dashboard, or the observability build id from getBuildId.

limit.description: Max sessions to return. Defaults to 10.

offset.description: Pagination offset for the REST session list.

status.description: Optional session status filter (e.g. done, running, error). Applied client-side.

tools.name: fetchSelfHealedSelectors
tools.description: Fetch BrowserStack self-healed selectors plus the test source code for the run. Provide exactly one of `sessionId` (single Automate / App-Automate session) or `buildUuid` (full self-healing report for a build). Pass the returned locator pairs to `prepareSelfHealingPlan` to plan edits. Requires a session id. listSessions lists them for a build; if you do not have the build either, getBuildId or listBuildId resolves one from a project and build name.

sessionId.description: Session ID. Mutually exclusive with buildUuid.

sessionType.description: Used with sessionId. Defaults to automate.

buildUuid.description: Build UUID. Fetches the build's self-healing report.

tools.name: prepareSelfHealingPlan
tools.description: Build a self-healing edit plan that bundles locator pairs with test source code for the calling LLM to apply with its own editing tools. This tool does NOT modify files — it returns structured context so the LLM can edit only the relevant call sites (avoids blind find/replace across shared ids/classes). `sessions` accepts the canonical shape `[{sessionId, locators: [{original, healed, thought?}]}]`, a single session object, an envelope `{sessions: [...]}`, the raw report `{healing_logs: [...]}` (with `healed_selectors` aliasing `locators`), and snake_case keys (`session_id`, `original_locator`, `healed_locator`, `healing_thought`). Requires a session id. listSessions lists them for a build; if you do not have the build either, getBuildId or listBuildId resolves one from a project and build name.

sessions.description: Sessions to plan edits for. See tool description for accepted shapes.

locators.description: Healed locator pairs for this session.

tools.name: fetchBuildInsights
tools.description: Fetch build details and quality gate results. Includes hashed_id and session_type for listSessions.

buildId.description: The build UUID of the BrowserStack build

tools.name: fetchRCA
tools.description: Fetch AI Root Cause Analysis for the current user's failed BrowserStack Automate/App-Automate tests. Suggests fixes only; never auto-apply, require explicit user approval. Requires test ids. Call listTestIds first if you do not have it.

testId.description: Array of integer test IDs to fetch RCA data for (maximum 3 IDs). These must be numeric test IDs, not session IDs or strings. If not provided, use the listTestIds tool to get all failed testcases. If more than 3 IDs are provided, only the first 3 will be processed.

tools.name: getBuildId
tools.description: Get the BrowserStack build ID for a given project and build name, scoped to the current user's builds.

browserStackProjectName.description: BrowserStack project name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

browserStackBuildName.description: BrowserStack build name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

tools.name: listBuildId
tools.description: Get the latest build ID for a project and build name, across all users (no user filter).

browserStackProjectName.description: BrowserStack project name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

browserStackBuildName.description: BrowserStack build name from the test run config (e.g. browserstack.yml). Exact match; no default.

tools.name: listTestIds
tools.description: List all tests of a BrowserStack build (each with its status and session id); optional status filter. Requires a BrowserStack build id. Call getBuildId or listBuildId first if you do not have it.

buildId.description: The Browserstack Build ID of the test run. If not known, use the getBuildId tool to fetch it using project and build name

status.description: Filter tests by status. If not provided, all tests are returned. Example for RCA usecase always use failed status

includeFailureDetail.description: Add per-test failure signature for clustering. Default false.

tools.name: askBrowserStackAI
tools.description: (Alpha, limited availability. Enabled per account and per product; if it is not enabled the call returns an entitlement error, nothing runs, and you should complete the task with the individual tools instead. To request access, the user should contact their BrowserStack account owner.) Use this when no other BrowserStack tool here fits the task, or when the ones you tried did not get you there. Prefer a specific tool whenever one fits: it is faster and more predictable than handing the job to an agent. Otherwise, describe what you want in plain language and BrowserStack's agent decides which calls to make, then returns its answer plus the steps it took. Anything that would change data pauses and asks you to confirm it first; deletes are refused outright. Put that confirmation to the user and answer with what THEY say — never decide on their behalf. If it cannot be put to anyone, the run is read-only and everything it wanted to change comes back in `needs_approval` instead. One task per call.

product.description: Which product to work in: tm (Test Management), tra (Test Reporting & Analytics).

query.description: What you want, in plain language. One thing per call.

decision.description: The user's answer. Never assume allow — ask them.

tools.name: listProducts
tools.description: List the BrowserStack products this surface can reach: what each one does, the entities it models, and a line saying what each entity is. START HERE — searchCapability needs a product, and this is what tells you which one. If two products could both fit the task, ask the user rather than choosing for them.

tools.name: describeEntity
tools.description: Describe one entity: what it is, what identifies it, what it relates to, and the vocabulary the product uses for it. Read this before filtering or writing, because ids and field values usually have to be resolved first.

product.description: Which product the entity belongs to: tm.

entity.description: Entity name, as listProducts returns it.

tools.name: searchCapability
tools.description: Find endpoints this surface can call, by plain language, within ONE product. You must say which: tm. If the task does not name it unambiguously, call listProducts first — it returns what each product does, the entities each models, and what every entity means, which is what settles the choice. Where two products use the same word for different things, ask the user rather than picking. Search matches the product's OWN words, not synonyms. When your words are not the product's, the response says so: `weak_match: true` with a `suggested_vocabulary` map of the product's entities and their aliases. Results are still returned, but treat them as unconfirmed — pick the closest entity from that map and search again using its vocabulary, or call describeEntity on it for the fuller picture. That one extra round trip is far cheaper than invoking the wrong capability. Narrowing further with `entity` sharpens results. THIS IS A SHORTLIST, NOT A CONTRACT. Each result carries only what you need to CHOOSE: `name` (the handle), `product`, `mode` (whether it writes), `intent` and `guidance` (what it does and what goes wrong), and `method`/`path` for products that publish no name yet. It does NOT carry parameters or response shapes. Once you have picked one, call describeCapability for its full contract, then invokeCapability. Fetching the contract only for the one you chose is the difference between ~1k and ~8.6k tokens a search. Results are ranked and capped. TO SEE EVERYTHING rather than search, pass query='*' — that lists the product (honouring `entity` and `mode`) in a stable order instead of ranking it, which is what you want when the task is 'what can this product do' rather than a lookup. TO PAGE, send `offset`: every response carries `offset` and, when more matched, `next_offset` — resend the SAME query with that value. `next_offset` is absent on the last page, so walk until it stops rather than comparing counts.

query.description: What you are trying to do, in plain language. Pass '*' (or 'all') to BROWSE instead of search: every capability in the product, in a stable order, paginated — use it when you want to see the surface rather than find one thing.

entity.description: Restrict to one entity (listProducts names them).

product.description: Which product to search: tm. Call listProducts if the task does not make it obvious, and ask the user when two products could both fit.

product_choice.description: 'user_confirmed' only when the user named the product, or the task names it unmistakably. 'not_asked' otherwise — then a query that could mean either product is refused and told what to ask, instead of being answered for the wrong one. Never search each product in turn and merge the results: that is the guess this argument exists to prevent.

mode.description: Restrict to reads or writes. Omit to let the query decide.

offset.description: Skip this many results — send the `next_offset` from the previous response with the SAME query to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: describeCapability
tools.description: The full contract for ONE capability you picked from searchCapability: its parameters grouped into path_params / query / body under the spec's own names, what it returns, and its declared response shapes fully expanded. Call this after search and before invokeCapability — search deliberately omits all of it, because it is only needed for the one capability you actually call. Identify it by `name`, exactly as search returned it; only when a result carries no `name` (some products publish none yet) pass `method` and `path` instead. Every parameter lists its type, whether it is required, its allowed values where the set is closed, and any limits the product declares — obey those before calling rather than discovering them from a rejected request.

name.description: The capability's published name, exactly as searchCapability returned it.

method.description: HTTP method — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

path.description: Path with {placeholders} intact — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

product.description: Which product owns it (tm). searchCapability returns it on every result; required only when two products share a name or a path.

include_responses.description: Which declared responses to expand: 'success' (default, the 2xx shape), 'all' (adds the error shapes — several times larger, and near-identical across endpoints), or 'none'.

tools.name: invokeCapability
tools.description: Call a capability whose contract you have from describeCapability. Pass `name` exactly as given — that is the handle. Only when a result carries no `name` (some products do not publish them yet) pass `method` and `path` instead, exactly as returned. Arguments go in path_params / query / body under the spec's own names. One call makes exactly one request and returns the product's own response untouched; when `completed` is false there is another page, which you fetch by sending the capability's own page parameter. If the mode is 'write' you MUST ask the user first, then resend with user_permission='granted' and a change_summary; both are recorded. Capabilities whose mode is 'destructive' (deletes) are refused outright — archiving, closing and merging are ordinary writes and DO run, so read the mode and intent before confirming with the user.

name.description: The capability's published name, exactly as returned (e.g. 'create_test_run_by_integer_id'). Preferred over method/path.

method.description: HTTP method — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

path.description: Path with {placeholders} intact — only for capabilities returned without a `name`.

body.description: Body fields, under the spec's names.

product.description: Which product owns the capability (tm). searchCapability returns it on every result; required only when two products share a name or a path.

user_permission.description: Set to 'granted' only after the user has confirmed a write.

change_summary.description: What will change. Required for writes.
